name: August 15, 2023 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 15, 2023
  VARIO US TELECONFERENCE LOCATIONS
  5:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Skophammer called the meeting to order at 5:34 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Dane Skophammer and Commissioners Georgia Goldfarb, Suzanne
  Guldimann, and Alicia Peak

  ABSENT: Vice Chair Cayley Jenner

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Kate Manisco,
  Recreation Manager; and Chris Orosz, Recreation Supervisor

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Skophammer led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Chair Skophammer seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda and to hear Item No. l .A. at the end of the agenda. The question
  was called, and the motion carried 4-0; Vice Chair Jenner was absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recreation Manager Manisco reported the agenda for the meeting was posted on
  August 11, 2023.

ITEM2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  At the request of Commissioner Guldimann, Community Services Director Riesgo
  provided guidelines for discussion during the Written and Oral Communications
  from the Public portion of the agenda. She stated that the Commission may not act
  on matters discussed and may ask brief questions, and items could be added to a
  future agenda by Commission consensus.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15, 2023
  Page 2 of 10

In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
that the two written correspondence items submitted by members of the public were
sent to the Commission and are available to interested parties upon request.

Robert Brinkmann stated several people experienced technical difficulties joining
and staying in the meeting and was concerned that people would not be able to
address the Commission. He stated that he represented the newly formed Malibu
Marlins Swim Club and requested the Commission's assistance in securing access
to the Malibu community pool before the fall season. He stated there had been a
complication during the vendor application process regarding the allocation of pool
space.

Commissioner Peak inquired how many students had registered with the Malibu
Marlins Swim Club and if the speaker had met the new swim coach for the
Seawolves.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Chair Skophammer stated that he heard Mr.
Brinkmann state they had 40 swimmers, but he did not know where they would
have registered since it was not through the City.

Commissioner Guldimann stated that further discussion should be suspended until
after the other public speakers were heard and then limited to whether the matter
should be placed on the next meeting agenda.

Chair Skophammer stated that further questions would be general and held until
after the remainder of the public speakers were heard.

Olea Brinkmann stated that she was a former Seawolves swimmer and was entering
seventh grade. She stated she moved to the Malibu Marlin Swim Club because she
did not want to be on a swim team run by a board that did not consider their
swimmers' opinions, and she enjoyed being coached by Erik Ran. She stated that
she needed to attend swimming practices for Independent Study Physical Education
(ISPE) program at Malibu Middle School. She requested the Commission's
assistance in giving their swim club the pool time needed for her athletic interest
and education.

In response to Commissioner Peak's inquiry, Mr. Brinkmann stated the Malibu
Marlins Swim Club registered swimmers because the City could not take
registrations. He provided Recreation Manager Manisco with signup sheets and
received checks demonstrating the swimmers' commitment to their club.

Gael Firth stated they were horrified that the coach was terminated without any
notification to the swimmers and implored the Commission to give the Malibu
Marlins Swim Club the swim times and pool lanes they needed.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15, 2023
  Page 3 of 10

  Viva Belie stated she served as a captain of the Malibu Seawolves and enjoyed
  being coached by Coach Ran. She stated that she was excited to join the Malibu
  Marlins and hoped the Commission could help them access the pool.

  Joe Sichta, Malibu Aquatics Foundation Communications Director, stated that it
  was a difficult time for everybody. He stated the Malibu Aquatics Foundation
  wanted to be respectful to everyone who supported Coach Ran and benefitted from
  his coaching. He stated that the Malibu Aquatics Foundation was a parent-led
  volunteer organization, and Coach Ran had not met goals over the past year and a
  half. He stated that a difficult decision was made to fulfill their responsibility to
  deliver a high-quality swim program. He stated that the new coach brought great
  energy and a strong desire to accomplish the goal of creating a strong swim
  program. He stated sharing time with another swim team would disrupt the team
  atmosphere and interfere with times the Malibu Aquatics Foundation had already
  been assigned.

  Robert Gold thanked the Commissioners for their time. He stated there was graffiti
  at the skatepark, and the police arrested the vandal a few weeks prior. He requested
  that the Commission provide input at the next meeting on the City's intended action
  to prevent the defacement of private property.

  Bill Sampson stated that he had been involved in youth swimming programs since
  1994 and started swimming again. He stated he did not have a stake in the Malibu
  Aquatics Foundation or the Malibu Marlins. He stated he was concerned about
  written statements related to the Malibu Aquatics Foundation. He stated the
  coach's termination was an employee/employer issue, and it would not have been
  appropriate to notify people beforehand. He stated that he thought Erik Ran did a
  good job of providing programming, but it was his understanding that certain
  employment goals went unmet, and a change was made. He stated that he was
  familiar with members of the Malibu Aquatics Foundation and was sure they
  wanted the best for their swimmers. He encouraged the swimming community not
  to be in discord with each other.

  Sue Murphy and Erik Ran were not present in the meeting.

MOTION  Chair Skophammer moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to
  place an item on a future agenda to discuss forming an ad hoc committee to review
  the field and pool allocation process.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated that she felt uncomfortable that the Commission
  may be dropped in the middle of an argument in which she did not have all the
  facts. She indicated she wanted to discuss the matter at the next meeting. She stated
  that she thought an ad hoc committee would be a good idea for a thorough
  understanding of the allocation of resources.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15, 2023
  Page 4 of 10

  Chair Skophammer agreed and stated that he did not have enough information to
  determine the level of Commission involvement regarding the dispute, what
  direction should be taken, or if there was anything that could be done. He stated
  that the matter should be placed on the meeting agenda to discuss what should be
  done in similar situations in the future. He stated that a decision on their request for
  pool space should not be rushed.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated that the times had already been allocated for the
  fall season.

  Chair Skophammer inquired of Community Services Director Riesgo if there were
  alternatives available that did not conflict with the established pool schedule, such
  as an opportunity for both teams to practice without sharing lanes.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated that the Commission was not supposed to discuss
  the matter because it was not on the meeting agenda.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Commissioner Guldimann amended the motion to include an item on a future
  agenda to discuss the pool accommodation request by the Malibu Marlins Swim
  Club and discuss forming an ad hoc committee to review the field and pool
  allocation process.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker of the motion.

  Commissioner Peak stated that the process would take time and the Malibu Marlins
  Swim Club would not have a resolution in the next several months.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried 4-0, Vice Chair Jenner
  absent.

ITEM3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Skophammer moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to approve
  the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Vice
  Chair Jenner absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the May 16, 2023 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Special meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthly Report
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August l 5, 2023
  Page 5 of 10

  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in June and July 2023.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Earth Friendly Management Policy Quarterly Report
  Recommended Action:  Receive and file a report on the Earth Friendly
  Management Policy activities and third and fourth quarter reports for the months of
  January to June 2023.

  Recreation Supervisor Orosz presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Guldimann thanked Recreation Supervisor Orosz and stated the
  quarterly report was encouraging.

  At the request of Community Services Director Riesgo, Recreation Supervisor
  Orosz discussed the Pepperdine University partnership. He stated that the City
  worked with Pepperdine professors to facilitate onsite science evaluations at
  Legacy Park and he would organize student volunteer groups for weed control and
  other projects.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Supervisor Orosz clarified that
  honeybee colonies were relocated from areas that could pose a danger to the public.
  He stated a professional bee biologist permitted through the State visited park sites
  and moved the live bees to a site with low population density.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, he stated that the bee colonies were not
  established and were moved with the queen. He stated that a report on their survival
  once relocated could be requested.

  Commissioner Peak thanked Recreation Supervisor Orosz and expressed her
  excitement about the partnership with Pepperdine University.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  that the question of whether the Earth Friendly Management Group should meet
  monthly, or every other month was something that a working group of City staff
  could determine internally.

  B.  Permanent Skate Park Restrooms
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15, 2023
  Page 6 of 10

Recommended Action: Review and provide feedback regarding the addition of
permanent restrooms as part of the Permanent Skate Park design.

Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated that the restroom facility was not part of the original skatepark design and
additional funding was added due to feedback received from City and County
agencies during the Coastal Development Permit (CDP) process. She stated that the
restrooms would be locked behind the skatepark gate, but parkgoers would have
access during the skatepark's open hours. At the request of Commissioner Peak,
she displayed the figure that showed the proposed restroom location.

In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Supervisor Orosz stated the footprint
was approximately 600 square feet, dependent upon whether there would be a one
or two-restroom facility.

Commissioner Guldimann stated that the facility should have two gender-neutral
stalls with a water fountain and the design should be simple.

Commissioner Peak indicated agreement with Commissioner Guldimann and
requested a water bottle filling station. She stated that the restroom could be used
by those utilizing the nearby baseball fields since the only restrooms were on the
other side of the park near the Michael Landon Center.

Commissioner Guldimann agreed that the park needed an additional restroom and
that the prefabricated design seemed like a solution that was not too expensive.

Chair Skophammer stated that he agreed with restroom design elements but
questioned if adding the restroom would affect the project's lengthy timeline. He
stated that further delay to the skatepark project should be avoided.

In response to Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
staff were working with the designers to add irrigation to the design, and hoped it
would not delay the project. She stated that staff were finalizing the addendum to
the environmental impact report (EIR).

Chair Skophammer inquired if adding water flow to the system would change the
EIR as it pertained to the wastewater allocation.

In response to Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo stated that
adding a restroom facility should be done during the skatepark design process and
would not cause an issue. She stated that the Public Works Department was
working on the wastewater allocation for City Council approval. She stated once
that approval was received, the restroom facility, square footage, and number of
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15, 2023
  Page 7 of 10

fixtures were the basic information needed to be added to the addendum with the
Planning Department.

In response to Chair Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo stated that
she would work with the Public Works Department to ensure the wastewater
allocation for the skatepark and snack shack projects was included in the request to
City Council.

Commissioner Goldfarb inquired whether restroom facilities would be considered
at both the skate park and the snack shack and if the two stalls were enough to serve
the area.

Commissioner Guldimann stated the park was grossly underserved with restrooms.

In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Commissioner Peak stated restrooms were
needed at the skatepark and snack shack because they serviced two different areas.

Chair Skophammer stated that having restroom facilities at the skatepark and snack
shack areas was essential so children did not have to cross the street to use the
facility. He agreed the park needed restroom facilities and that four stalls were not
excessive. He stated he preferred to review the skatepark and snack shack projects
before voting. He stated that he did not want the inclusion of a restroom at the
skatepark to preclude a restroom at the snack shack.

Commissioner Peak stated that she understood Chair Skophammer' s concern but
stated the Commission should make a recommendation based on the information
staff presented. She stated the irrigation design was pending, so the restroom should
be added simultaneously.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated the
Public Works Department did not anticipate issues with the wastewater allocation.
She stated that the goal was to get approval for a wastewater allocation for the
skatepark and the snack shack facilities.

Commissioner Guldimann stated that modem facilities used less water, and the
Commission should add the skatepark restroom, with the goal of restrooms at both
locations. She stated a two-stall restroom would be convenient should a plumping
failure occur.

In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated that the difference in cost depended on the desired customization.

Commissioner Guldimann stated the restroom should be simple and surrounded by
beautiful landscaping.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15, 2023
  Page 8 of 10

  Commissioner Goldfarb agreed it would be desirable to include a water bottle
  refilling station and water fountain and inquired what the cost difference would be
  for the basic unit without customizations.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the cost was approximately $80,000 for a single unit and $160,000 for a
  double unit without customizations. She offered to provide more detailed
  information about wastewater allocation at the next meeting.

  Commissioner Peak stated staff heard the Commission's concerns and agreed to
  include restrooms within the skatepark plans.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated the Commission could have a second review ifthere
  were concerns following feedback from the Public Works Department.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated two additional toilets would not be a significant
  wastewater load, especially since there were not enough restrooms to serve the
  number of patrons using the facility.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated that from a sanitation point of view, a restroom
  by the snack shack was necessary because they served food, and it made sense to
  have a restroom with sinks nearby for families to wash their hands

MOTION  Commissioner Peak moved, and Chair Skophammer seconded a motion to
  recommend a prefabricated gender-neutral double restroom facility with a baby-
  changing station in each restroom, a water bottle filling station, and a drinking
  fountain not exceeding 600 square feet, provided the wastewater allocation did not
  preclude the installation of a restroom and sink for the snack shack. The question
  was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chair Jenner absent.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Recreation Manager Manisco provided an update on Parks and Recreation Month
  activities, department program interest and satisfaction surveys, and Senior Needs
  Assessment. She provided an overview of the Fall Recreation Guide and usage
  priorities for aquatics programs.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Manisco stated that
  the pool schedule would be provided at the September 19, 2023 Regular meeting
  in addition to the data requested during public comment.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Recreation Manager Manisco stated that the
  City coordinated the evening Masters Program at the pool. She stated the morning
  Masters Program was a facility rental facilitated through the school district.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15, 2023
  Page 9 of 10

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the
  Malibu Marlins Swim Club rented the facility through the school district. She stated
  the pool could be rented from the District from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. on the
  weekends.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Recreation Manager Manisco stated the City
  had too many evening Master Swimming Program registrants to share swimming
  lanes with the Malibu Marlins Swim Club and that the time allotted to the
  Seawolves was too full to accommodate a second club within the pool.

  Community Services Director Riesgo invited questions about the swim clubs to be
  directed to staff before the next meeting, and information would be added to the
  staff report.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated that she appreciated everyone's efforts. She
  encouraged the swimming clubs to consider sharing the pool space.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated she participated in a volunteer weed-pulling effort
  at the Point Dume Headlands, organized by Poison Free Malibu. She stated the
  program was important because it helped the State Parks Department change its
  weed control methods from chemical herbicides. She announced an upcoming
  volunteer weed-pulling event on September 15, 2023. She stated that it was a
  testament to the City's commitment to be poison-free, which was spreading to other
  agencies.

  Commissioner Peak thanked everyone for everything they do and stated the public
  comments and controversy regarding pool usage illustrated the need for an aquatics
  center. She stated that Mr. Gold needed to address the issue with Public Safety and
  the Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department. She encouraged swimmers from the
  Malibu Marlins Swim Club to train with the new Seawolves coach in the interim
  so the swimmers would not lose training time. She expressed her frustration with
  Farmers Market vendors using plastic bags and stated the Cornucopia Foundation
  should be responsible for their vendors following the rules. She recommended the
  Earth Friendly Management Group explore the use of goats for brush clearance.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  staff had researched brush clearance with goats, and it was approximately three
  times the cost of using mowers and hand-held equipment.

  Commissioner Peak stated she was approached by numerous seniors wanting a
  dedicated Senior Center space and suggested developing the outdoor patio area for
  their use.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of August 15 , 2023
  Page IO of 10

  Chair Skophammer stated that the pool situation reiterated the need for an aquatics
  center.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Commissioner Goldfarb stated goats were
  problematic and would eat young native plants, which defeated the purpose of
  passive restoration for native plants.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENT A TIO NS

  A. Election of Chair and Vice Chair

  This item was not heard and continued to the September 19, 2023 Regular meeting.

  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  None.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 6:58 p.m. , Commissioner Chair Skophammer moved, and Commissioner
  Guldimann seconded a motion to adjourn the meeting. The question was called,
  and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chair Jenner absent.

  Approved and adopted by the Parks and
  Recreation Commission of the City of
  Malibu o January 16, 2024.
